newsitem.title: USA: US RAIL INTERMODAL VOLUME UP FROM YR AGO-AAR.
newsitem.headline: US RAIL INTERMODAL VOLUME UP FROM YR AGO-AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal volume rose in the week ended August 2 from the same 1996 week, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR reported a total of 173,957 trailers and containers in the week, up 5.7 percent from 164,551 in the year-ago week. Intermodal volume does not include carloads.

It said carloads in the week totaled 342,069, down one percent from 345,678 a year ago, while ton-miles fell 0.4 percent to 26.2 billion from 26.3 billion last year. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.

Among carloads, AAR said that farm products other than grain plunged 24.5 percent last week to 1,005 from 1,332 in the year-ago week, while nonmetallic minerals loadings fell 6.5 percent to 9,122 from 9,752.
Coal loadings also declined 6.4 percent to 126,513 in the week from 135,209 a year ago.
But carloads of petroleum products climed 10.2 percent in the August 2 week to 5,971 from 5,417 a year ago, while motor vehicles and equipment rose 9.4 percent to 19,773 from 18,069.

In the first 31 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal volume rose eight percent to 5.07 million trailers and containers from 4.69 million in the same 1996 period. Carloads rose 1.3 percent to 10.5 million from 10.4 million, while ton-miles rose 1.7 percent to 813.6 billion from 799.8 billion in the year-ago period, AAR said.

Separately, AAR reported that U.S. carloads on the two Canada-based railroads had 52,162 carloads in the August 2 week, up 4.5 percent from the year-ago week, and 25,297 trailers and containers, up 12 percent from a year ago.

Combined U.S. carload volume in the United States and Canada-based railroads for the first 31 weeks of 1997 totaled 12.1 million, up 1.5 percent from the same 1996 period, and 5.82 million trailers and containers, up 8.4 percent from the year-ago period, AAR said.

AAR also said that for the month of July, combined U.S. intermodal rail freight on U.S.- and Canada-based railroads rose 9.5 percent from July 1996, while carloads increased 1.1 percent from the year-ago month.
